messages.subject: Question about saveWave function
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone, I have an issue with the saveWave function : everything works well, it creates a .wav file, but I can't use this file in python and some other softwares, most of the time I have the error "wrong wav format".

May be an issue with the audio codec ? Is there a way to change it ?

Best regards,

Léo P.

Hello Léo,
I guess you mean seewave::savewav().
This function mainly uses tuneR::writeWave()
I could open without error messages .wav files saved with seewave::savewav() with audacity under ubuntu 18.04.
Does any one have a similar experience as Léo with python in particular?

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Question about saveWave function
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have had this issue before in Python, I think it was related to opening wav files with a sample rate of over 48kHz, and it was only when using the default Python wave.open().

The solution was to use scipy.io.wavfile.read().

I have just checked this again with a 96kHz sampled file exported from tuneR and it gives “wrong wav format” with wave.open() and works fine with the scipy method. I have not investigated further but it looks like this might be an issue with base Python rather than tuneR/seewave.

Best,

Ed
